data.description:
## Why
An orchestrator that creates many unfocused workspaces mounts a live SwiftUI tree for each of them. The mount cap rises with the pending set, so the cap never holds. Backlog item: B012.

## Evidence
origin/main `0ff8887e5e`, verified in `reconcileMountedWorkspaceIds`.

- `Sources/ContentView.swift` (the function at about 3029-3051) unions `pendingBackgroundWorkspaceLoadIds` into `pinnedIds`, then sets `maxMounted = max(baseMaxMounted, selectedCount + pinnedIds.count)`. The base cap is 1. The pending set defeats it.
- Callers pass `eagerLoadTerminal: !focus` when creating a workspace that should not be focused (`SocketDispatch` near the workspace-create handler). Re-find that call. Fable cited `SocketDispatch.swift:1303` on this SHA.
- Upstream cmux #7182 (`802351c879`) caps concurrent background mounts and still allows the headless start a new terminal needs.
- Research: Fable cluster C5, wave 1. This is a producer for the SwiftUI hangs in C11-197, C11-202, and C11-205. It is not a sidebar rewrite.

## Scope
In: pending background loads do not raise `maxMounted` without a small fixed ceiling. Workspaces still get created. Their terminals still start headless when something sends or reads. They do not all mount their SwiftUI bodies at once.

Out:
- Wakeup coalescing (B030), title filtering (B061), and the layout flush (B056). Separate tickets.
- Sidebar snapshot isolation (B059). Gated on the soak. Do not start it here.
- Dropping unfocused workspace creation to "enforce" the cap. Astra: do not cap pending work by dropping launches.
- Parked B038 (initial split ratios). Re-check only if you are in that layout path. Do not expand.

## Approach
Give background mounts a constant ceiling, in the spirit of upstream's policy type, and keep the selected workspace and a real handoff pair outside that ceiling. Headless terminal start stays on the existing bootstrap path. Do not mount a workspace just because its terminal is starting.

## Acceptance criteria
1. A socket script creates 20 workspaces without focusing them. The number of mounted workspace bodies stays at or under the ceiling. `tree` still lists all 20.
2. `send` to a terminal in one of those unfocused workspaces still runs, via the headless start, without mounting every sibling.
3. The workspace the operator is looking at stays mounted. Cycling workspaces still shows the one they selected.

## Validation
A logic test for the mount-id function if it is pure (`WorkspaceMountPolicy.nextMountedWorkspaceIds` already looks pure). Feed it 20 pending ids and assert the mounted set size. Then one tagged-build socket script for criterion 2, on Atlas after C11-216. No soak. No source-grep test. Computer use: glance that the focused workspace is the one on screen, not a blank sidebar.

## Dependencies
None inside ws:bugs. The cold-start ticket is related: headless start must keep working under the cap. Do not block on it. Cross-workstream: F1 is C11-216. The lead links it. C11-197, C11-202, and C11-205 stay the hang records. This ticket is one producer.

## Risks
A ceiling that prevents a background agent from starting at all. The acceptance send is the guard. Typing latency: this removes mounted trees. It must not add work to `TabItemView` or `hitTest`. Doctrine: no tenant config. No new strings. `TabItemView`'s `Equatable` stays untouched.

Size: S. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: mount accounting only.
data.title: Cap how many background workspaces mount at once

provenance.reason: c11 1.0 bug cluster depends on F1

C11-301 review handoff

Draft PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/514
Head: e6c893cd11 (linked branch c11-1.0/C11-301-mount-cap)
Base: 14fd85a5a6, fetched origin/main including C11-296.
Plan: .lattice/plans/task_01M3X6K2A53E4THPWD9W0M9ARP.md

Observed: `git diff --check` and `python3 -m py_compile tests_v2/test_background_workspace_mount_cap.py` pass. These are patch/syntax checks, not behavioral execution. GitHub CI pending; owner will monitor and record actual WorkspaceMountPolicyTests results. No local Swift builds, no production socket testing, no tagged runtime or timing claims.

Scope: ContentView has a contained admission helper, reconcile replacement, and publisher-value forwarding. One pending background body is allowed beside selected and real retiring IDs (2 normal / 3 during handoff / 1 settled). Debug fixture retention stays explicitly outside that cap. Requests, workspace models, existing headless startup, two-second prime timeout and typing/input/focus paths are unchanged. Publisher emission is used directly because @Published sends before property storage changes. C11-260 can independently change sidebar ContentView code.

Validator scenario (batch runtime gate authorized by Orchestrator; explicitly use 60 workspaces for the 50+ request):
1. Build tagged baseline and merged candidate on Atlas, QA fresh, with debug pin-retention fixtures OFF. Record exact SHAs, host load, source/tag/socket/log identity and display conditions. If C11-259 holds the Atlas slots, wait for remote-build.sh to resume; slot queuing is not a blocker. Use the isolated guest/sandbox socket route, never the operator session.
2. Run c11Tests/WorkspaceMountPolicyTests and inspect the individual results (the enclosing host suite is advisory). Seven new tests plus the nine existing tests must pass. They exercise 20 pending loads, stable admission during handoff, deleted/deduplicated selection, complete 60-ID queue promotion, all 60 selections from a cold mount cache, and debug-retention exemption. Completion and timeout remove the same pending ID; the policy test verifies promotion rather than claiming to exercise the timeout timer.
3. In the isolated tagged app, run tests_v2/test_background_workspace_mount_cap.py with explicit C11_SOCKET_PATH and C11_MOUNT_LOG=/tmp/c11-debug-<tag>.log. The test creates 60 unfocused workspaces and checks real ws.mount.reconcile events: <=2 bodies without handoff; selected is always included; all 60 model UUIDs remain listed. It reads and sends a synthetic marker to a later actually unmounted workspace, then requires unchanged original selection/focused tab. Every queue member must finish (ready or existing timeout), and mounts settle to exactly one. It switches first/middle/last/original and requires <=3 bodies during handoff and one after settlement. Save the DEBUG event interval and printed elapsed time. No inference from model count alone.
4. Separately create and retain 60 synthetic workspaces for restore validation (the script above cleans up its own batch). Include terminal-only workspaces and one selected workspace with a readable split. While priming remains in progress, use the real tagged UI to select first/middle/last and then cycle all 60. Check the selected workspace UUID against socket state, readable visible terminal content, absence of persistent blank panels, preserved split ratios, and no input-active retiring workspace. Capture screenshots of first/middle/last and the selected split. Confirm mount-log bounds during switches and settlement. Do not edit the split/layout implementation under this ticket.
5. Record all 60 workspace UUIDs and the selected split layout; gracefully quit only this tagged test app to save its session, then relaunch the same tag with QA resume. Expect all 60 UUIDs/layouts restored. Cycle all 60 again; verify selected body/content each time, <=3 mounts during real handoff/priming, and exactly the selected body after settlement. Read/send synthetic markers to restored background targets without selecting them; check their output and unchanged current selection. Capture restore and post-cycle logs/screenshots.
6. Run the same creation/switch/restore workload on tagged baseline, record peak actual mounted bodies, creation/settlement/switch timings and load average for both. No dedicated soak or measured typing-latency claim from this owner. Clean up only test workspaces/app. Any computer use enumerates displays first, is confined to the verified tagged app/display, has a 20-minute hard timer and proves dismissal with synthesized input before closeout.

No new strings, persisted schema or installed-skill changes. No edits to sidebar rows, TabItemView, hitTest, forceRefresh, Ghostty wakeups or layout flush. Shared B012 already has an upstream cmux #7182 fix; this patch reuses c11 mechanisms. Review routed only by Orchestrator; no merge by owner.

# C11-301 review, cycle 1

Verdict: **PASS (static code review)**

PR #514. Head `e6c893cd119730137808f0d2e2c5836799d83d67`; base `14fd85a5a6e68878fca6e009619d953188eb2471` (merge-base with fetched origin/main). Reviewed the whole three-file diff, ticket, plan, validation comment, repository policies and the unchanged creation, priming, handoff, restore, terminal lifetime and sidebar projection seams. Checkout and PR head agree; review checkout is clean. No builds, tests or app-driving runs performed by this reviewer.

## Blocking

None found.

The production admission overload bounds pending background mounts to one, independently of queue size. It preserves an existing selected workspace and a genuine retiring workspace, deduplicates those against pending admission, retains the admitted pending load, and promotes the next queued workspace after removal. Debug fixture pins remain an explicit exemption. Reconciliation consumes the emitted pending set rather than the pre-update @Published property. The existing two-second timeout and headless demand paths remain intact.

Unmounting removes presentation trees without deleting Workspace/TerminalTab models or freeing their owned terminal runtime. Sidebar notification, agent-state and flag projection reads those models and stores independently of the mounted content subset. Selection inserts a cold workspace into the mount set; existing presentation rules keep only the selected workspace input-active. The patch does not change TabItemView equality, input/hitTest/forceRefresh paths, telemetry threading, persistence schemas, tenant configuration or user-facing strings. New Swift tests execute the production admission policy; the socket fixture reads runtime events and terminal output rather than source text.

## Non-blocking

1. `tests_v2/test_background_workspace_mount_cap.py:95`: strengthen the per-switch oracle. If socket selection changes for first/middle/last but the presentation never reconciles, the loop checks only workspace.current; the later check can accept the pre-switch settled event for the original workspace. Thus the script can report successful switch settlement without observing those intermediate mounts. Smallest improvement: after each select, wait for a fresh reconcile sample naming that target and containing its mount ID. This is non-blocking because the separately required batch UI scenario explicitly checks each selected body's visible content, including all 60 workspaces.

## Runtime proof still required

The owner's validation comment `ev_01M3XNRDYN71HE0RPYQQ9JT2QS` records patch/syntax checks and a future Validator scenario, not executed behavioral evidence. The plan explicitly batch-defers tagged runtime acceptance for this ticket; that authorized deferral does not block this static verdict. It does not establish product acceptance.

Before landing, the captain must gate on green exact-head CI and inspect the individual results for all 16 WorkspaceMountPolicyTests (seven new, nine existing). At the final review snapshot, the build check was queued and macOS compatibility tests were in progress; neither is reported as passing.

The Atlas batch Validator must execute the documented isolated tagged-app baseline/candidate scenario with debug retention disabled:

- Run the 60-workspace socket fixture: retain all workspace models, observe at most two mounts during background priming and three during a genuine handoff, promote the entire queue through ready/timeout completion, and settle to the selected body alone.
- Read/send to an actually unmounted later queue member, observe executed synthetic output and unchanged selection/focused tab, and preserve existing terminal output/scrollback. Confirm agent status, notifications and flags still reach its sidebar row while its content is unmounted.
- Use the real tagged UI to select/cycle all 60 workspaces during creation and after graceful shutdown/QA resume. Verify restored UUIDs and split layout, readable selected content, no persistent blank panels, no input-active retiring workspace, and mount bounds during switches and settlement.
- Record exact baseline/candidate SHAs, host load, mount logs, creation/settlement/switch timings and screenshots. Enumerate the validation display, enforce the stated timer and prove dismissal. Runtime validation and release sign-off remain outstanding.
